Consult Summary:
- Young adult with 2 months of progressive morning-predominant anxiety related to a new stressful job with associated insomnia, daytime impairment, palpitations, low mood, and reduced enjoyment of activities; plan: offer talking therapy referral/self-referral resources, sleep advice, arrange basic blood tests for palpitations, and GP follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Progressive anxiety for ~2 months, worst in mornings, causing marked dread of leaving house and going to work.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately two months ago, coinciding with starting a new job in retail head office.
  - Symptoms have progressively worsened over those months.
- Exacerbating / initiating / relieving factors:
  - Likely initiated/coincided with starting a new job; boss described as "not very nice" and work perceived as very stressful.
  - Public transport (tube) and crowded/airless environments worsen anxiety.
  - No specific relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Sleep: difficulty falling asleep, very shallow sleep, estimates 3–4 hours/night; awaken early with palpitations and racing heart.
  - Cardiovascular: palpitations, described as irregular and sometimes prolonged (minutes up to ~10 minutes); sometimes painful sensation in chest when heart racing; patient worried it might be a heart problem.
  - Mood: low mood, loss of enjoyment in previously enjoyed activities (running, tennis), low energy.
  - Appetite: no significant change in regular eating; increased chocolate consumption.
  - Social: avoidance of social activities at times; still has social support (family).
  - Suicidal ideation: denies suicidal thoughts or intent.
  - Substance use: drinks alcohol more than usual on Fridays/Saturdays and has a glass of wine sometimes during the week; occasional smoking; denies recreational drug use.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No history of prior similar episodes of this severity.
  - No prior panic attacks that prevented her attending work.
  - Denies current suicidal ideation or intent.
  - No specific medical diagnoses reported by patient.

Past Medical History:
- No past medical conditions disclosed in the consult.
- Family history: mother has a history of depression.

Medications:
- No regular medications documented.
- No medication doses or prescriptions discussed.
Allergies:
- No allergies documented.

Social History:
- Lives with parents.
- Employment: recently started new job (head office team) for a fashion retailer; first job in retail; reports workplace stress and poor relationship with boss.
- Alcohol: increased intake on weekends ("quite a lot" on Fridays/Saturdays); occasional glass of wine during the week offered by parents; exact quantities not documented.
- Tobacco: occasional smoking.
- Recreational drugs: denies use.
- Hobbies/exercise: previously ran and played tennis but has decreased participation due to low mood/anxiety.
- Support system: reports good family support.

Family History:
- Mother with history of depression.
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented.
- Vitals: not provided.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed during the consult.
- Plan documented to perform "a couple of basic blood tests" to exclude triggers for palpitations (tests not specified and not yet done).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Anxiety symptoms (work-related, >2 months) with functional impairment
  - Assessment:
    - Anxiety symptoms described as persistent, morning-predominant, worsened since starting a new job; associated with excessive worry, avoidance, reduced enjoyment, and daytime impairment.
  - Plan:
    - Offer talking therapy: patient agreeable to one-to-one therapy.
      - Patient advised she can self-refer via NHS for talking therapy; doctor to send link.
      - Provide online resources for immediate use while waiting for service.
    - Advise to contact GP/Babylon support line if anxiety worsens to the point of inability to cope with work or daily activities.
    - Medication for anxiety mentioned as a possible option in future but "not suggested in the first instance."
    - Add information to medical record regarding sleep management strategies (doctor will place sleep advice on notes).
- Issue 2: Insomnia / disturbed sleep
  - Assessment:
    - Difficulty initiating sleep and early morning awakenings due to anxiety and palpitations; estimated sleep 3–4 hours/night causing daytime fatigue.
  - Plan:
    - Provide sleep hygiene / sleep pattern advice (doctor to add guidance to notes).
    - Monitor response to therapy and sleep advice; reconsider further interventions if not improving.
- Issue 3: Palpitations, irregular, associated with anxiety
  - Assessment:
    - Palpitations are temporally associated with anxiety and panic-like awakenings; patient concerned about possible cardiac cause.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange basic blood tests to exclude physiological triggers (tests not specified in consult).
    - Arrange GP follow-up approximately one week after blood tests to review results.
    - Patient instructed to call support line to arrange blood tests.
    - Reassure probable anxiety-related cause but investigate as above.

- General plan items:
  - Provide self-referral link for NHS talking therapy and online resources.
  - Documented plan to add sleep advice to the record.
  - Safety net: advise patient to re-contact if symptoms worsen or if she becomes unable to cope; explicit escalation if suicidal ideation develops (patient currently denies such thoughts).
